what: NetApp makes data storage systems and the software that manages data across on-premises hardware and the public clouds. Its cloud storage services run natively inside Amazon, Microsoft and Google's platforms.
customers: Large enterprises, government agencies and cloud providers storing and managing data.
money: storage systems, software and support contracts
cloud storage services sold through the major cloud providers
moat: Storage operating software that enterprises build their data management around, and a unique position as first-party storage inside all three big clouds.
risks: Storage hardware growth is slow in a mature market
Memory and component cost increases squeeze margins
Public cloud revenue has grown more slowly than hoped
Revenue grew only about 5% last year
opportunities: Return on invested capital of 32% with a 71% gross margin
AI workloads need large amounts of fast storage, which is its core product
Cash of about $3.6 billion exceeds its debt, funding buybacks
watch: All-flash array revenue and public cloud services growth.
